_comment: THE POSTURE TABLE. One scan implementation, two placements (st_dd0e19d8 AC15/AC16).
This file is DATA, not code, and that is the whole point: if a blocking class ever
produces a false positive on ordinary product vocabulary, the recovery is to change
one word here from 'block' to 'report' — no code edit, no redeploy of the gate.
That escape hatch is failure-manifest entry 1 of the design and it is the reason
the owner's commits cannot be held hostage by this gate.
PLACEMENTS
staged   every commit (pre-commit, scans only the staged files)
publish  the publication certification run (scans the whole tree / published set)
VALUES
block    a non-permitted finding of this class fails the run
report   the finding is printed and the run still succeeds
skip     the class is not scanned at all in this placement, and the run summary
SAYS SO — an exclusion that is reported rather than invisible
PROMOTION RULE (how a class earns 'block' at commit time). A class is set to block
at 'staged' only when (a) it already blocked at commit before this story — relaxing
that is a regression — or (b) a full-tree run shows zero non-permitted findings for
it. Every class below records which of the two applies and, where it is still
reporting, the measured finding count that has to reach zero first.
SKIP_PATHS KINDS (required on every entry — the loader rejects an entry without one).
gate_source            code or config the gate must not flag itself on. It carries NO
corpus term, ever. Nothing in the gate can check that, because
the gate does not scan these files — so it is checked OUT OF BAND
by scripts/qa/skip-paths-corpus-proof.js, which scans them against
the corpus with separator variants and with the local allowlist
un-suppressed. QA st_dd0e19d8 found a real leak in one of them.
self_match_dictionary  a list the gate matches AGAINST. Scanning it flags its own
entries by construction, so the out-of-band proof asserts instead
that every finding is one of the file's own DATA entries — a term
appearing in a comment or any non-entry position still fails.
Adding a skip path without a kind fails the table load, which fails every run that
reads it. That is the point: a new exclusion cannot escape the out-of-band scan.
NO OWNER DATA IN THIS FILE. It names classes and repo paths, never terms.

terms._why: Tier A — the owner's distinctive terms from the gitignored config overrides. This POSTURE has been block-at-commit since st_e36f5f2b and relaxing it is a regression; what changed is the corpus, not the policy. Measured 2026-07-25: the pre-story term set (58 terms, no surface variants) found 0 findings on the whole tree; phase 1's AC12 singular/plural rule adds the one form that matches, and it finds 1 — scripts/ingest/03b-service-vendor.js, a company name stored plural and written singular. That is precisely the leak AC12 exists to catch and AC1 removes, so it blocks. Consequence to know about: that one file cannot be committed until AC1 edits it, which is the edit phase 3 already makes.

private_terms._why: AC9 — the owner's name, family, stored contacts, work colleagues and archive slugs. Same precision class as Tier A, but NEVER scanned at commit before this story, and measured 2026-07-25 at 35 findings across 11 tracked files. Blocking those at commit would fail ordinary commits on work this story has not done yet. Promote to block when the count reaches zero (AC1/AC5, phase 3).

entity_ids._why: Content-id suffixes of real people/companies/places. LOOKED like it blocked at commit since st_e36f5f2b; measured 2026-07-25, it caught nothing at all. Its shape carried a \b word boundary, which git's POSIX engine reads as a literal 'b' — so the arm matched 'b' followed by 16 hex characters (12 files, none of them containing a real id) instead of matching ids. Phase 1 fixed the shape, and the fixed arm found 7 genuine leaks across 3 files. PROMOTED TO BLOCK 2026-07-26 on the owner's decision ("Turn them on"), against the promotion rule's condition (b): re-measured on the whole tracked tree after the phase 3 removals, the fixed arm finds ZERO findings — permitted or otherwise. Nothing is being suppressed to reach that number: the permitted list carries no entity_ids entry at all, and it cannot (the class is owner-identifying, so LOCAL_ONLY_CLASSES refuses it in the tracked half). Proven at commit placement, not only on the tree: scripts/qa/commit-posture-proof.js stages the files the pre-commit de-tax itself regenerates and asserts exit 0.

emails._why: AC11 — real addresses from the owner's graph, matched by shape + set intersection. Never scanned at commit before this story. Measured 2026-07-25: 38 findings across 17 files, of which 21 were two public-by-construction addresses and 17 were genuine leaks in 4 files. PROMOTED TO BLOCK 2026-07-26 on the owner's decision ("Turn them on"), against the promotion rule's condition (b): re-measured on the whole tracked tree after the phase 3 removals, 21 findings across 13 file/term pairs remain and ALL 21 are permitted — the non-permitted count is zero. THE CONDITION THE OWNER'S DECISION CARRIED: 8 of those 21 rows sit in 5 files the pre-commit hook REGENERATES AND STAGES during the commit (public-truth.js, public-truth.json, llms-full.txt, faq-bundle.js, faq-context.json), so the hook itself puts the address back on every commit. Without a permitted entry for each, this promotion would fail every commit the owner makes. All 13 pairs are seeded in config/publication-permitted.json and the seeding is proven at commit placement by scripts/qa/commit-posture-proof.js, which stages those regenerated files and asserts exit 0.

domains._why: AC11 — domains of companies the owner is part of, scoped to employers. Never scanned at commit before this story. Measured 2026-07-25: 1 finding, in a generic vendor-domain list. It is an owner decision under AC5 whether that is a leak or a permitted collision, so this build does not pre-empt it.

literal_names._why: AC10 — company, place, alias and person names from the entity graph: 24,253 patterns, the measured-noisy class (217 findings across 66 files). SKIPPED at commit on COST, not on policy. Measured 2026-07-25 on this tree: this pattern file costs a 1.17s FLOOR before any haystack is read (1.26s over one staged file, 2.11s over a realistic de-tax staged set, 2.07s with apps/static/llms-full.txt alone) against a 1.5s budget for everything pre-commit adds. Scanning it at commit breaks the budget on an ordinary commit. It blocks at publication, where a one-off 24s full-tree pass is affordable. Reversing this needs a token-index scan family for names, not a posture change.

paths._why: A corpus term baked into a tracked FILE PATH leaks even when the contents are clean. Scan family rather than a corpus class: it matches the terms + private_terms literals against path strings. Has blocked at commit since st_e36f5f2b. Measured 2026-07-25: 0 findings.

skip_paths.reason: the gate's own CLI facade — a gate that can block on its own source can block every commit
gate source (corpus assembly) — same exclusion as the facade, not a new class
gate source (corpus extraction) — same exclusion as the facade
gate source (scan families) — same exclusion as the facade
gate source (posture + permitted list) — same exclusion as the facade
gate source (permitted-list CLI) — same exclusion as the facade
this file — it names the classes the gate hunts, so it must not be hunted
the permitted list holds, by construction, terms that already appear in the tree; scanning it would flag every entry it exists to excuse
the gitignored half of the permitted list — same reason, and it never ships
the allowlist catalogs the collisions the corpus must ignore; scanning it flags its own contents
AC19 bulk dictionary — 25,005 surnames. The gate cannot scan the dictionary it matches against without matching itself.
AC19 bulk dictionary — 2,164 nicknames, same self-match problem
AC19 bulk dictionary — 5,862 startup domains, same self-match problem
